title: Produce a researched VCF 9 migration architecture for a consolidated management estate
prompt:
Produce the migration architecture for the estate in `fixtures/estate.json`. This is an architecture deliverable, not an explanatory report. Implement it by replacing the placeholder `migrationplan/architecture.json` with one JSON document that conforms exactly to `installer/architecture.schema.json`. The document must cover every inventoried source product at its exact version, map it to the requested VCF 9 target component, order the migrations, give every inventoried content/configuration item exactly one carry-forward or abandonment disposition, include the gates required by the selected path, and state the source version's end-of-general-support boundary. Include the placement and per-node sizing of every target component in the single-site consolidated management domain; the design must fit the four-host minimum represented by the fixture. Use `installer/compatibility-snapshot.json` as the pinned grading authority for paths, compatibility, order, gates, sizing, and support dates.

Before finalizing the artifact, use the harness's real network research capability to consult Broadcom-published sources for the supported migration paths, content/configuration compatibility, product support boundaries, target sizing, and the minimum host design. Do not treat the pinned snapshot as a substitute for that live research. Record the Broadcom pages you actually consulted in `research.sources`, including title, URL, consultation date, and the claims each source informed. Choose the sources and searches yourself; no particular URL or query is prescribed.

The existing fixture, installer specification, compatibility snapshot, Go module, package loader, schema validator, and verifier are protected inputs and must remain unchanged. Keep the implementation self-contained and deterministic. Run `go test -race ./...` to verify the result.

network.reason: The task requires genuine research against currently reachable Broadcom migration, compatibility, lifecycle, sizing, and management-domain design publications; deterministic verification itself is offline.
